items.label: AIWA language list
items.detail: Confirm the person’s language and interpreter availability with AIWA; the list does not establish availability in each health region.

blocks.do: Make space to get to know each other
blocks.why: The social yarn builds connection before focusing on health concerns.

blocks.do: Invite the person to tell their health story
blocks.why: The diagnostic yarn listens to their account and connects it with the clinical assessment.

blocks.do: Work towards a shared understanding of the plan
blocks.why: The management yarn uses understandable explanations and discussion to agree the way forward.

items.label: Read the clinical yarning paper
items.detail: A communication approach from Lin, Green and Bessarab; adapt to the person, not a universal cultural script.

blocks.do: Ask who they would like with them
blocks.why: The Act names family and community members, including elders.
blocks.say: Is there someone you would like with you while we talk?

blocks.do: Offer an Aboriginal mental health worker
blocks.why: The Act asks for collaboration with Aboriginal mental health workers where practicable.
blocks.say: Would you like an Aboriginal mental health worker to join us?

blocks.do: Use words that make sense to them
blocks.why: The Act says communication must be in terms the person is likely to understand.
blocks.say: Tell me if I use a word that does not make sense.

blocks.do: Ask about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander identity; do not infer it from appearance
blocks.why: WA Health explains why this is asked of everyone. Record an answer only in the authorised clinical record, never in PsychSift.

blocks.do: Use an interpreter if one is needed
blocks.why: The Act asks for an interpreter where necessary and practicable.

blocks.heading: Cultural safety
blocks.text: Cultural safety is decided by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, families and communities, not by the clinician.

blocks.heading: Wellbeing is whole
blocks.text: Social and emotional wellbeing covers body, mind, family, community, culture, Country and spirit.

blocks.do: Ask who in the family should be involved
blocks.why: The Act asks services to have regard to the views of the family.
blocks.say: Who in your family should we talk with?

blocks.do: Ask about elders
blocks.why: The Act names elders among the community members to work with.
blocks.say: Is there an elder you would like us to involve?

blocks.do: Let the person and family say who counts as family
blocks.why: Cultural safety is decided by the person, their family and community.

blocks.do: Ask whom the person wants involved in treatment discussions
blocks.why: Involving family supports discussion; it does not itself establish authority to consent.

items.label: Consent policy and decision-maker guidance
items.detail: Use the current policy for capacity, consent and substitute decision-making requirements.

blocks.do: Ask the person and family what visiting would help
blocks.why: Care should fit cultural practice and the views of the family.

items.label: Family and domestic violence guidance
items.detail: Official WA Health resources for staff, including screening, referral and safety guidance. Follow your service’s current procedure.

blocks.heading: Mental Health Act 2014 (WA), section 81
blocks.text: To the extent that it is practicable and appropriate to do so, the examination of a person who is of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent must be conducted in collaboration with — (a) Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander mental health workers; and (b) significant members of the person's community, including elders and traditional healers.

items.title: Offer an Aboriginal mental health worker
items.detail: Involve them where practicable and appropriate.

items.title: Ask about family, elders or healers
items.detail: Ask the person who they want involved.

items.title: Check language
items.detail: Use an interpreter if needed and practicable.

blocks.heading: Culture is not illness
blocks.text: Under the Act, holding a cultural belief or taking part in cultural activity does not by itself mean a person has a mental illness.

blocks.heading: Information from others
blocks.text: Information from an Aboriginal mental health worker or community member can inform the examination, but the Act says an order cannot rest on that information alone.

blocks.heading: What to record
blocks.template: Examined in collaboration with [blank] (Aboriginal mental health worker) and [blank] (family or community member), in line with s 81.

items.label: National SEWB framework
items.detail: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mental health and social and emotional wellbeing

blocks.do: Ask the person and family what matters to them in their care
blocks.why: Cultural safety is decided by the person, their family and community.

blocks.do: Ask whether they would like an elder or traditional healer involved
blocks.why: The Act names elders and traditional healers among those to work with, where practicable and appropriate.

blocks.do: Ask about home and Country
blocks.why: Connection to Country is part of social and emotional wellbeing.

blocks.do: Reflect on your own assumptions and power in the room
blocks.why: The national definition of culturally safe practice includes ongoing critical reflection and care free of racism.

blocks.avoid: Relying on a phone interpreter for a mental health interview
blocks.instead: Book an on-site or video interpreter; Aboriginal Interpreting WA for Aboriginal languages.

blocks.avoid: Assuming English is the person's first language
blocks.instead: Ask which language they are most comfortable in.

blocks.avoid: Deciding for the person who counts as family
blocks.instead: Ask the person and family who should be involved.

blocks.avoid: Reading a cultural belief or practice as a sign of illness
blocks.instead: Remember the Act: culture alone does not mean mental illness. Ask the Aboriginal mental health worker for context.

blocks.avoid: Examining without offering an Aboriginal mental health worker
blocks.instead: Offer one and involve them where practicable (s 81).

blocks.avoid: Assuming you know what the person needs culturally
blocks.instead: Ask. Cultural safety is decided by the person, their family and community.

items.title: Involve family and the Aboriginal mental health worker
items.detail: Have regard to the family's views in the plan.

items.title: Explain the plan in words they understand

blocks.do: Offer 13YARN for support after discharge
blocks.why: A crisis line for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, open 24 hours.

blocks.do: Ask whether they are registered for the Closing the Gap PBS co-payment
blocks.why: It lowers what eligible Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people pay for PBS medicines.

blocks.do: If they live in the country, check whether PATS can help with travel
blocks.why: PATS is WA Country Health Service's travel and accommodation subsidy for country patients.

blocks.do: Offer follow-up with their local Aboriginal community controlled health service
blocks.why: AHCWA is the peak body for these services across WA.

items.label: Find an AHCWA member service
items.detail: Community-controlled services listed by area; confirm the appropriate service with the person.

items.label: AHCWA publications
items.detail: Browse Aboriginal-produced resources with the person. Selection of a local patient resource pack still awaits the Aboriginal health team.

blocks.do: Involve family and the Aboriginal mental health worker early
blocks.why: The Act asks services to have regard to the family's views and to work with Aboriginal mental health workers.

blocks.do: Ask whether being on Country matters to the person and family
blocks.why: Connection to Country and spirit is part of social and emotional wellbeing.

blocks.do: Ask the family what they need; do not assume rules
blocks.why: Cultural safety is decided by the family and community.

items.label: Coroner information for families
items.detail: Official information about the coronial process, counselling and contacting the Court. Check with the Court about requests concerning the person who has died.

phrases.say: Would you like an Aboriginal mental health worker to be with us?
phrases.why: The Act asks for collaboration with Aboriginal mental health workers where practicable.

phrases.say: Is there someone you would like with you while we talk?
phrases.why: The Act names family and community members, including elders.

phrases.say: Which language would you like to talk in?
phrases.why: The Act says communication must be in a language the person is likely to understand.

phrases.say: Can I ask an Aboriginal mental health worker to come and talk with us?
phrases.why: The Act asks for collaboration with Aboriginal mental health workers where practicable.

phrases.say: Is there someone in your family you would like us to call?
phrases.why: The Act asks services to have regard to the views of the family.

phrases.say: Would it help to talk in your own language, with an interpreter?
phrases.why: Aboriginal Interpreting WA is the primary language service for Aboriginal people in WA.

phrases.say: Who in your family should be part of this talk?
phrases.why: Cultural safety is decided by the person, their family and community.

phrases.say: Would you like an elder or someone from community here too?
phrases.why: The Act names elders among the community members to work with.

phrases.say: Shall we book an interpreter to be here in person?
phrases.why: WA Health guidelines say phone interpreting is not suited to sensitive mental health talks.

phrases.say: I want to explain what the Mental Health Act means for you, in words that make sense to you.
phrases.why: The Act says communication must be in terms the person is likely to understand.

phrases.say: Would you like an Aboriginal mental health worker with us for this examination?
phrases.why: Section 81 asks for the examination to be in collaboration with Aboriginal mental health workers where practicable.

phrases.say: Is there an elder or traditional healer you would like us to involve?
phrases.why: Section 81 names elders and traditional healers.

phrases.say: Is anything happening in your family or community right now that we should know about?
phrases.why: Family and community are part of social and emotional wellbeing.

phrases.say: What do you need from us so you can take part in family and cultural business?
phrases.why: The Act asks for care that fits the person's cultural and spiritual practices.

phrases.say: Who in your family should we talk with about this?
phrases.why: The Act asks services to have regard to the views of the family.

phrases.say: Where is home, and how will you get there?
phrases.why: PATS can help country patients with travel and accommodation costs.

phrases.say: Do you have a local Aboriginal health service you would like us to link with?
phrases.why: AHCWA is the peak body for Aboriginal community controlled health services across WA.

phrases.say: Are you registered for Closing the Gap help with medicine costs?
phrases.why: It lowers what eligible people pay for PBS medicines.
